product: Large-frame and small gas turbines (GTCC), steam power, light-water nuclear reactors and nuclear fuel, defence and space systems, commercial aircraft structures, commercial ships, metals machinery, engines and large chillers, plus a data-centre and energy-management business moved into the renamed Industrial Solutions segment on 2026-04-01.
demand: Order intake is at record levels: Q1 FY2026 order intake JPY2.0224tn and order backlog above JPY14tn, with large-frame gas-turbine backlog at 35GW versus 23GW a year earlier, driven by US and Asian data-centre and utility demand. The CFO said demand is broadly in line with, or slightly above, expectations.
pricing_power: Strong. CFO Nishio said on 2026-08-06 that in the large-frame turbine market and core US utility segment there has been no change in the strong supply-demand environment or in the trend of improving profitability on new orders. Large-frame turbines are sold out through 2028, and after-sales services are described as highly profitable.
competition: Mainly GE Vernova and Siemens Energy in large-frame gas turbines, both running record backlogs and long lead times; Siemens Energy reported a record EUR136bn backlog after 194 turbine sales in 2025. Domestically Kawasaki Heavy Industries and IHI compete in defence, while Chinese OEMs compete in steam power, metals machinery and commercial ships.
team: President and CEO Eisaku Ito; CFO Hiroshi Nishio; Masayuki Eguchi is Corporate Executive Vice President and head of the Defence and Space segment. The 101st Annual General Meeting of Shareholders was held 2026-06-26 and the FY2025 securities report was filed 2026-06-24.
market_strategy: Execute the 2024 Medium-Term Business Plan: roughly double large-frame gas-turbine capacity versus 2024, stay selective with core US utility customers, grow high-margin after-sales, and build AI and autonomy capability through the Preferred Networks alliance while partnering with NEC on defence command and control and unmanned systems.
bull: Q1 FY2026 (2026-08-04) order intake JPY2.0224tn record; large-frame gas-turbine backlog 35GW vs 23GW; Energy Systems orders +56% YoY; sold out through 2028; FY order-intake guidance raised to JPY7.0tn.
bear: FY2026 order-intake guidance cut ~8.5% vs FY2025; Q1 profit up 65% leaned on JPY25bn one-time and JPY9bn FX; USD3.2bn exposure at JPY150/USD; Aircraft/Defense orders fell; two Sell ratings.
falsifier: Any FY2026 quarterly disclosure showing order intake below the JPY7.0tn guidance run-rate, or a guidance cut, e.g. at the Q2 FY2026 results due early November 2026.
web_what_changed: Q1 FY2026 (2026-08-04): record order intake JPY2.0224tn, revenue JPY1.1942tn, business profit JPY159.6bn, net income JPY134.6bn; large-frame gas-turbine backlog 35GW vs 23GW a year earlier. web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No fresh earnings, filing or guidance change dated yesterday.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Demand and volume led: Energy Systems order intake rose 56% YoY to JPY1.3593tn on GTCC, with 10 large-frame gas turbines ordered in Q1 (4 US, 6 Japan). Price/mix also helped: of a JPY55bn profit bridge, JPY38bn was margin improvement (JPY25bn one-time) and JPY17bn revenue, with new-order profitability improving.
web_suppliers: Not found. No supplier names or named supplier constraints appeared in the sources read. Management instead points to its own production capacity, saying it is doubling large-frame gas-turbine capacity versus 2024, is sold out through 2028, and is still evaluating whether more capacity is needed.
web_customers: Core US utility customers (contracted selectively), Japanese utilities (6 of 10 Q1 large-frame turbine orders) and Asian industrial and data-centre buyers; Japan Ministry of Defence for defence; commercial aviation OEMs. Highly concentrated: Energy Systems booked JPY1.3593tn, about 67% of the JPY2.0224tn Q1 order intake.
web_who_loses: Large-frame gas-turbine rivals GE Vernova and Siemens Energy lose share and pricing power to a selective MHI. In defence, Japanese primes such as Kawasaki Heavy Industries and IHI lose share as MHI and NEC target command, control and unmanned systems. Chinese steam-power and shipbuilding OEMs lose metals-machinery and commercial-ship orders.
web_contradicting_evidence: FY2026 order-intake guidance was cut JPY653.6bn versus FY2025 to JPY7.0tn, down about 8.5%, so bookings are normalising. Q1 business profit up 65% YoY leaned on JPY25bn of one-time gains plus JPY9bn weak-yen FX. FX exposure is USD3.2bn at a JPY150/USD assumption, so yen strength reverses gains. Aircraft/Defense Q1 orders fell on a high base, and stockanalysis lists one Sell and one Strong Sell rating.
web_if_management_right: FY2026 delivers revenue JPY5.4tn, business profit JPY540bn and net income JPY380bn; CFO Nishio said on 2026-08-06 that results may exceed guidance because JPY55bn of an expected JPY83bn revenue-plus-margin benefit already landed in Q1. Backlog above JPY14tn converts through 2028-2030 as capacity doubles versus 2024.
web_if_management_wrong: Yen appreciation against the JPY150/USD assumption breaks the profit bridge first, given USD3.2bn FX exposure. Next is long-cycle plant execution risk: the JPY15bn Q1 gain came from finally settling a previously unsettled contract price under percentage-of-completion. Middle East and other geopolitical impacts are explicitly excluded from guidance, and the raised dividend would be at risk.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Preferred Networks gains a JPY10bn MHI investment plus deployment of its AI in mission-critical machinery; NEC gains a defence digital-sovereignty partner. Further out: Japanese gas-turbine castings, forgings and component suppliers; US utilities and data-centre developers that locked 2028-2030 turbine slots; Japanese defence electronics and unmanned-systems supply chains; MHI after-sales service partners.
